Rashi on Bava Kamma 48b:18:1.english: The one who taught this, etc. - The first clause [follows] the Rabbis, and the latter clause [follows] Rabbi.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 48b:19:1.hebrew: כולה רבי היא - וסיפא דוקא. ורישא לא תידוק מינה: הא סתמא הוזק — חייב, דודאי סתמא נמי הזיק — חייב, הוזק — פטור. והאי דנקט "ושמרו", לחיוביה נזק שלם קאמר אם הוזק שורו של בעל חצר, הא סתמא — חצי נזק:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 48b:19:1.english: The entire [baraita] is [in accordance with] Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] - And the latter clause is exact. And [from] the first clause, do not infer from it [that] if [the ox entered] without specification [and] was damaged, [the courtyard owner] is liable; for certainly [if it entered] without specification as well, [if it] caused damage, [its owner] is liable, [and if it] was damaged, [the courtyard owner] is exempt. And that which [the baraita] stated, "and safeguard it," it says [this] to obligate him [for] full damage if the courtyard owner's ox was damaged, whereas [if it entered] without specification — [he pays] half-damage.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 48b:1:1.hebrew: הזיקו - בידים זה את זה, ואפי' שלא במתכוין:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 48b:1:1.english: They injured - one another directly [lit., with their hands], and even unintentionally.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 48b:1:2.hebrew: או שניהן שלא ברשות - כגון שניהן רצין ברה"ר:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 48b:1:2.english: Or both of them without permission - For example, both of them are running in the public domain.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 48b:1:3.hebrew: חייבין - דבנזקין לא שני לן בין מתכוין לשאין מתכוין. והא דתנן בהמניח (לעיל בבא קמא דף לב.): "שנים שהיו מהלכין ברה"ר והזיקו זה את זה פטורין", ההוא "הזיקו" "הוזקו" הוא, ולא דק בלישניה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 48b:1:3.english: They are liable - For with regard to damages, we do not distinguish between one who intends [to cause damage] and one who does not intend [to cause damage]. And [as for] that which we learned in a Mishnah in [the chapter] HaMeniach (above, Bava Kamma 32a): "Two [people] who were walking in the public domain and damaged one another are exempt" — that [term] "damaged" [hiziku] means "were injured" [huzku], and [the Tanna] was not precise in his phrasing.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 48b:1:4.hebrew: דברשות פטור - בין היזק דבידים בין היזק דממילא, ובדלא ידע ליה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 48b:1:4.english: [The one] with permission is exempt - Both [in a case of] damage [done] with [his] hands and [in a case of] damage [that occurs] on its own, and [this applies] where he did not know of him.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 48b:22:1.hebrew: שור שהיה מתכוין לחבירו - הוא הדין למתכוין לאשה נמי פטור, כדאמרינן בפירקין דלעיל (בבא קמא דף מב.) נקי מדמי ולדות. ובגמ' מפרש אמאי נקט מתכוין לחבירו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 48b:22:1.english: An ox that was intending [to gore] another [ox] - The same law [applies] where it intended [to gore] a woman: it is also exempt, as we say in our chapter above (Bava Kamma 42a), "[He is] clear of [paying] compensation for offspring." And in the Gemara, it explains why [the Mishnah] used [the case of] "intending [to gore] another."

Rashi on Bava Kamma 48b:2:1.english: Where it contaminated [the water] at the time of the fall - For it is an actual damager, and is not similar to a pit.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 48b:2:2.hebrew: ומים כלים - כל חפצים ככלים, דלא חייב בבור (עלה מיתה אלא על נזקי בהמה), ושאר חפצים, הזיקן זו היא מיתתן:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 48b:2:2.english: And the water [has the status of] utensils - All objects are like utensils, for [the Torah] did not impose liability in [the case of] a pit (for death, except for damages to an animal), and [as for] other objects, their damage is [considered] their death.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 48b:3:1.hebrew: מאי איכא למימר - הא לית ליה תורת בור, וממונו הוא, ומשורו למדנו, ולא פטר ביה כלים:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 48b:3:1.english: What is there to say - Behold, it does not have the legal status of a Pit, and it is his property, and we derive [its law] from his ox, and [Scripture] did not exempt utensils in it.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 48b:4:1.english: With its body - [Meaning] that it was soiled with mud.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 48b:4:2.hebrew: אבל מריחיה - לאו גופיה הוא, דסרחון דנבילה ממילא אתי לה, ונבילה גרמא הוא שגורמת לסרחון שיבא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 48b:4:2.english: But from its stench - it is not its body [itself], for the stench of the carcass comes about on its own, and the carcass is [merely] an indirect cause, as it causes the stench to come.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 48b:6:1.hebrew: בר קטלא הוא - בנפילה קמייתא, והיאך בא לידי מועד? בשלמא גבי מועד דנגיחות איכא למימר כדאמרינן בפירקין דלעיל (בבא קמא דף מא.): דקטל וערק, א"נ בשאין מכירין את השור, אי נמי שהוזמו זוממי זוממין. אבל זה לא עלה מן הבור מאליו, וליכא למימר ערק, ולא אין מכירין, ולא הוזמו, דמילתא דאית ליה קלא היא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 48b:6:1.english: It is liable to be put to death - With the first fall, so how did it come to be a forewarned [ox]? Granted, regarding a forewarned [ox] for goring, one can say as we said in the previous chapter (Bava Kamma 41a): that it killed and fled, or else where they do not recognize the ox, or else where the refuting [*zomemim*] witnesses were themselves refuted. However, this [ox] did not climb out of the pit on its own, so one cannot say it fled, nor [that] they do not recognize [it], nor [that the witnesses] were refuted, for it is a matter that is widely known.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 48b:6:2.hebrew: דחזא ירוקא - עשב על פי הבור, ובא לאכול ונפל, דאהך נפילה לא איכוין. ומיהו, כופר שלא בכוונה משלם בנפילה אחרונה, ואע"פ שאין השור בסקילה. ושמעינן לרב (לעיל בבא קמא דף מד.) דאמר פטור מזה ומזה — ה"מ במועד לנגיחות בכוונה, וערק לאגמא בראשונה ונגח ד' שלא בכוונה, פטר ליה מגזירת הכתוב, דכתיב השור יסקל וגם בעליו וגו', כל זמן שאין השור בסקילה אין בעלים משלמין כופר. אבל זה, שלא היתה בו חיוב סקילה כלל, אין העדאתו אלא לכופר של שן ורגל בחצר הניזק, דאוקמינן ברגל שדרסה ע"ג תינוק בחצר הניזק דאיכא כופר ברגל, ואף על גב דשלא בכוונה הוא ואין השור בסקילה. וה"נ, דחזא ירוקא ונפל, תולדה דשן היא, דמתכוין להנאתו. וא"ת משונה הוא ואין זו שן — כיון דאייעד ליה, אורחא הוא. ולאוקמי להך נפילה אחרונה במתכוין והשור בסקילה לא מצינן, דלגבי כוונה תם הוא וליכא כופר, דהא כל כמה דלא חזי ירוקא לא אייעד:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 48b:6:2.english: Where it saw grass - [i.e.,] grass at the mouth of the pit, and it came to eat [it] and fell, so that it did not intend this fall. Nevertheless, [its owner] pays ransom [for killing] unintentionally on the final fall, even though the ox is not [subject] to stoning. And [as for what] we learned regarding Rav (above, Bava Kamma, daf 44a), who said [that the owner is] exempt from both this [death] and that [ransom] — that applies only to [an ox] forewarned for goring intentionally, which fled to the marsh at first and gored a fourth [time] unintentionally; [there, Rav] exempted him by a scriptural decree, as it is written: "The ox shall be stoned, and also its owner [shall be put to death]" etc. — as long as the ox is not [subject] to stoning, the owner does not pay ransom. However, this [ox], which never had a liability of stoning at all, its forewarning is only for the ransom of [the category of] *Shen* (Tooth) and *Regel* (Foot) in the injured party's courtyard — as we established regarding a foot that trampled upon an infant in the injured party's courtyard, where there is ransom for *Regel* even though it is unintentional and the ox is not [subject] to stoning. And here too, where it saw grass and fell, it is a derivative (*toladah*) of *Shen*, since it intends [to act] for its own pleasure. And if you say: it is unusual [behavior], and this is not [the normal manner of] *Shen* — once it has been forewarned for it, it is [considered] its [normal] way. And we cannot establish this final fall as intentional, with the ox [subject] to stoning, because with respect to intent it is a *tam* (unforewarned), and there would be no ransom, for as long as it does not see grass it is not forewarned.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 48b:7:1.hebrew: ושמואל אמר - לעולם בתם, ומתניתין חצי כופר קאמר, ור' יוסי היא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 48b:7:1.english: And Shmuel said - In fact, [it is dealing] with an innocuous [ox], and our Mishnah means half a ransom, and it is [the opinion of] Rabbi Yosei.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 48b:8:1.english: Ulla - [He] also establishes it [as referring] to an innocuous [ox] and [paying] a full ransom.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 48b:9:1.hebrew: היינו דקתני אביו או בנו - דהוי קרן בחצר הניזק דמשלם כופר שלם. אלא לשמואל דאמר חצי כופר, מאי איריא כו':
Rashi on Bava Kamma 48b:9:1.english: This is [why] it teaches: his father or his son - For it is [a case of] Horn in the courtyard of the injured party, where [the owner] pays full ransom. But according to Shmuel, who says [he pays] half-ransom, why specifically [his father or his son], etc.?

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 48b:14:1.hebrew: טעמא דאמר ליה שמרו - כולה הך סוגיא כרבא דלעיל, דלר' זירא לא קשה כלל רישא לסיפא, וכולה רבי היא, והוי סתמא שניהם פטורין בין ברישא בין בסיפא, דאין כל אחד מקבל עליו שמירת חבירו; ולרבנן, הא סתמא שניהם חייבים:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 48b:14:1.english: "The reason [is] that he said to him, 'Safeguard it'" - This entire sugya follows Rava above; for according to Rabbi Zeira, the first clause does not contradict the last clause at all, and the entire [baraita] is [the view of] Rabbi [Yehudah HaNasi], and in an unspecified case both of them are exempt, both in the first clause and in the last clause, since neither one accepts upon himself the safeguarding of his fellow's [property]; whereas according to the Rabbis, in an unspecified case both of them are liable:

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 48b:15:1.hebrew: אימא סיפא כו' - הכא לא משני "נעשה", כדמשני בפרק קמא דקדושין (דף ה:) גבי "נתן הוא ואמרה היא מקודשת; נתנה היא ואמר הוא אין מקודשת", משום דהכא אית ליה שנויא אחרינא, דקאמר "תברא"; אבל התם ליכא למימר "תברא", דליכא פלוגתא במילתא:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 48b:15:1.english: Say the latter clause, etc. - Here [the Gemara] does not answer "it is considered [as if...]," as it answers in the first chapter of Kiddushin (5b) regarding [the case of] "If he gave [the betrothal money] and she said [the betrothal formula], she is betrothed; if she gave and he said, she is not betrothed" — because here it has another answer, as it says tavra [i.e., the two clauses are contradictory and reflect different Tannaic opinions]; whereas there one cannot say tavra, because there is no [Tannaic] dispute in the matter.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 48b:16:1.hebrew: טעמא דאמר ליה שמרו - כולה הך סוגיא כרבא דלעיל; דלר' זירא לא קשה כלל רישא לסיפא, וכולה רבי היא, והוי סתמא שניהם פטורין בין ברישא בין בסיפא, דאין כל אחד מקבל עליו שמירת חבירו, ולרבנן הא סתמא שניהם חייבים:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 48b:16:1.english: The reason is that he said to him, "Safeguard it" - This entire sugya follows Rava [cited] above; for according to Rabbi Zeira, the first clause does not contradict the latter clause at all, and the entire [baraita] is [the opinion of] Rebbi, so in an unspecified case both are exempt, both in the first clause and in the latter clause, since neither one accepts upon himself the safeguarding of his fellow's [property], whereas according to the Rabbis, in an unspecified case both are liable.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 48b:1:1.hebrew: שניהם ברשות - פ"ה: כגון ברה"ר, שלא ברשות — כגון ששניהם רצים ברה"ר. וקשה, דהיינו מתניתין בפרק המניח (לעיל בבא קמא דף לב.)! ונראה לפרש: כגון שנכנס לחצר בע"ה שלא ברשות או ברשות, דאית ליה לאסוקי אדעתיה: כמו שנתנו לו רשות, כמו כן נתנו לאחר רשות; או כמו שהוא נכנס שלא ברשות, שמא גם אחר נכנס שלא ברשות. ולכך חייבין כשהזיקו זה את זה, אפי' הזיקו שלא מדעת. אבל אחד ברשות ואחד שלא ברשות — האי אית ליה לאסוקי אדעתיה בהאי, והאי לית ליה לאסוקי אדעתיה בהאי; ואם שלא מדעת הזיקו, ברשות פטור, שלא ברשות חייב:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 48b:1:1.english: "Both of them with permission" - Rashi's explanation: [This refers to a case] such as in a public domain; [and "both of them] without permission" — such as where both of them are running in a public domain. And this is difficult, for that is [already taught in] the Mishnah in the chapter [entitled] HaMeniach (above, Bava Kamma 32a)! Rather, it appears [correct] to explain [that it refers to a case] such as where one entered the courtyard of a homeowner without permission or with permission, for it should occur to him [that] just as they gave him permission, so too they gave another permission; or [that] just as he entered without permission, perhaps another also entered without permission. And therefore they are liable when they injured each other, even if they injured unintentionally. However, [in the case of] one with permission and one without permission — this one [without permission] should have had this one [with permission] in mind, whereas this one [with permission] does not have to have this one [without permission] in mind; and [therefore] if they injured unintentionally, the one with permission is exempt, [and] the one without permission is liable.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 48b:6:1.hebrew: דחזא ירוקא ונפל - רש"י מוקי ההיא דהיה מתחכך בכותל: בג' פעמים הראשונים לא היתה כונתו להתחכך, אלא בכוונה להפיל על האדם; ופטור דקתני התם — אהך אחרונה שהיתה להתחכך, והראשונות אהנו שנעשה מתוך כך מועד. ובהך אחרינא חשיב ליה משונה קצת שהרג בנפילת הכותל, ולכך לא נחשב מועד אלא מחמת הראשונות. וזהו דוחק, דחשיב משונה מה שעושה להנאתו, לאכול ירוקא או להתחכך. וגם תימה הוא לומר דהוי מועד בהפלת כותל אחרונה שהיתה שלא בכוונה, על ידי הראשונות שהיו בכוונה. ולפירושו צ"ל דהא דקאמר הכא "במועד ליפול על בני אדם בבורות", לא הזכיר בני אדם אלא בשביל אחרונה, דבג' הראשונות לא חיישינן אלא שיהא מועד ויעשה אורחיה להפיל עצמו בבור לאכול הירק:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 48b:6:1.english: Where it saw grass and fell - Rashi interprets that [baraita] of "it was rubbing itself against a wall": in the first three times, its intention was not to rub itself, but rather [it acted] intentionally to knock [the wall] down upon the person; and [the ruling] "exempt" that is taught there [refers] to this last [incident], which was [merely] to rub itself, while the first [three incidents] were effective in that it thereby became forewarned. And in that other [case], he considers it somewhat unusual that it killed through the falling of the wall, and therefore it is not considered forewarned except on account of the first [incidents]. But this is forced, that he considers unusual what it does for its own pleasure — to eat grass or to rub itself. And it is also astonishing to say that it becomes forewarned for the last knocking down of a wall, which was unintentional, by means of the first [incidents], which were intentional. And according to his explanation, one must say that [regarding] what [the Gemara] says here, "With [an ox] forewarned for falling on people in pits," it only mentioned people because of the last [fall], for in the first three [falls] we are only concerned that it become forewarned and that it become its normal habit to throw itself into a pit to eat the grass.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 48b:7:1.hebrew: ושמואל אמר הלכתא כרבי - לכאורה נראה דהלכתא כשמואל בדיני, וצ"ע: דרבא קאמר לעיל: "הכניס שורו לחצר בעל הבית שלא ברשות וחפר בו בורות שיחין ומערות — בעל השור חייב בנזקי חצר", משמע אבל ברשות פטור; ואי כרבי, אפי' ברשות חייב, דלרבי סתמא חייב בעל השור. וכולה סוגיא דלעיל מסיק רבא כרבנן, ואפי' נשברו ברוח ואפי' חנק עצמו:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 48b:7:1.english: "And Shmuel said: The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi]" - At first glance it appears that the halakha is in accordance with Shmuel in monetary matters, yet this requires further study: for Rava said above: "[If] one brought his ox into the homeowner's courtyard without permission and it dug pits, ditches, or caves in it — the owner of the ox is liable for the damage to the courtyard," [which] implies that [if he brought it in] with permission, he is exempt; whereas if [the halakha is] in accordance with Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi], he is liable even [when entering] with permission, for according to Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi], the owner of the ox is liable in an unspecified case. And [throughout] the entire sugya above, Rava concludes in accordance with the Rabbis — even [where] they broke in the wind, and even [where] it strangled itself.
